title: The Last Stand at Glenrowan
style: Style: 1880s Australian Bush BalladInstrumentation: Solemn, driving acoustic guitar, haunting fiddle, and a slow, heavy kick drum like a heartbeat.
lyrics: (Verse 1)It was June of eighteen-eighty at the Ann Jones’ local Inn,With the railway torn to splinters to do the trap-train in.But the traps survived the gully, and they pinned my brothers down,So I strapped on ninety-seven pounds of steel to take the town.Forged from beaten plough-shares, a mouldboard for a chest,I slipped out through the ironbark to put them to the test.(Verse 2)The Monday fog was freezing as I flanked the police line,With a heavy Colt revolver and a vengeance by design.I stepped out from the clearing and I struck my iron helm,The ringing echoed like a bell across the Murray realm.I rested one hand on my hip, a towering tin-clad man,And marched straight at the rifle-fire to end what we began.(Chorus)And Sergeant Steele was roaring, "Push the townsfolk well away!Keep the gawkers past the station-yard and hold them all at bay!"They watched me from the railway siding, frozen in the chill,The last man of the Kelly breed, descending on the hill.A monster made of mouldboards, with my hand upon my side,Taking every ounce of lead the peeling rifles could provide.(Verse 3)Superintendent Hare was bleeding, dragged away before the dawn,Now fifty guns were turning on the devil on the lawn.They fired Martini-Henrys, and I laughed to feel the blow,"Fire away, you dogs, you cannot hurt me!" I let the troopers know.The bullets sparked and ricocheted into the morning wood,While the hostages watched breathless from the windows where they stood.(Verse 4)It was the paramount, exact moment—the climax of the fray,A standoff in the clearing where the smoke turned black to grey.I stood my ground untethered, a sovereign of the bush,Defying all Victoria in the morning's deadly hush.But a bushman’s got no armor where the iron doesn't reach,And Steele aimed for my unprotected legs to force the breach.(Outro)The shotgun tore my thighs apart, the heavy iron crashed,The armor stained with Kelly blood, the wild rebellion smashed.The townsfolk watched in silence as they stripped me on the grass,The last stand at Glenrowan in the broken, bloody glass."Such is life," I whispered, as they dragged me to the train,An iron king of Victoria, returning to the chain.
